title: DA Hike: Understanding Dearness Allowance Types and Calculation
description: Dearness Allowance (DA) is a component of salary paid to government employees and pensioners to offset the impact of inflation. It is calculated as a percenta.

faq.q: What is the primary purpose of Dearness Allowance?
faq.a: The primary purpose of Dearness Allowance is to compensate government employees and pensioners for the erosion of their purchasing power due to inflation and the rising cost of living.

faq.q: How often is Dearness Allowance revised?
faq.a: Dearness Allowance for Central Government employees (VDA) is typically revised twice a year, effective from January 1st and July 1st. For PSU employees (IDA), revisions are often quarterly.
Yes, Dearness Allowance is fully taxable. It is added to your total income and is subject to income tax as per the applicable slab rates.

faq.q: What is the difference between IDA and VDA?
faq.a: IDA (Industrial Dearness Allowance) is for Public Sector Undertaking (PSU) employees, while VDA (Variable Dearness Allowance) is for Central Government, State Government, and Union Territory employees. Their calculation methods and revision frequencies can differ slightly.

faq.q: What is the CPI-IW and why is it important for DA calculation?
faq.a: The CPI-IW (Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers) is an economic indicator published by the Labour Bureau. It measures changes in the retail prices of goods and services consumed by industrial workers and is crucial because DA calculation formulas are directly linked to its movements.

faq.q: Can DA be merged with basic pay?
faq.a: Yes, historically, when DA reaches a significant percentage (e.g., 50%), the government has sometimes merged it with the basic pay. This is done to ensure that the effective salary remains substantial and to avoid a very high DA percentage.
For Central Government employees, the Ministry of Finance notifies the DA rates. For Public Sector Undertaking employees, the Department of Public Enterprises (DPE) issues guidelines.
